transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-29
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 50m
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE), Dr. Mira Patel (Lynwood Head of ML), Evan Torres (Lynwood CTO), Janelle Kim (Procurement)

Summary (auto): quick renewal check-in, discussing capacity top-up for EU and Ireland on-prem option, contract amendment timing, security checklist follow-ups, plan pilot for dedicated capacity.

[00:00:05] Alex (AE): hey everyone, appreciate you carving out time. quick agenda — renewal timeline, capacity bump for EU region, onprem/vpc option for Ireland, and next steps. ok?
[00:00:18] Dr. Mira Patel: yep, sounds good. short on time today so we'll hit the highlights.
[00:00:25] Evan Torres: morning all. from our side procurement questions too, so janelle might chime in.
[00:00:32] Janelle Kim: thanks. i have the current contract on screen. aiming to lock numbers by mid-oct if possible.
[00:00:40] Samir (SE): great. quick refresh — currently you're on Redwood Hosted with ~120k tokens/day, latency SLO at 250ms p50 for chat flows, and you've been experimenting with prefix caching and light quantization. correct?
[00:00:53] Dr. Mira Patel: yes mostly. the big ask is to add EU capacity — specifically ireland nodes — and a small dedicated pool for PHI workloads. also curious about private onprem for a future phase.
[00:01:05] Alex (AE): cool. so two asks: 1) capacity top-up in EU region, 2) dedicated VPC/onprem pilot for PHI. we usually separate those in pricing but can fold into a single amendment if timeline works.
[00:01:20] Evan Torres: cost is a factor. latency matters but we need the private pilot for compliance. what are the trade-offs on latency vs cost if we go dedicated vs Hosted with VPC?
[00:01:33] Samir (SE): short answer: dedicated gives you consistent tail latency and KV-cache locality which helps repeated convo contexts — so better p95. hosted with VPC peering can be cheaper initially but you'll see more variability and potential egress hop. also quantization choices matter — int8 quantization can lower cost but sometimes adds 5-15ms.
[00:01:50] [00:02:10] Dr. Mira Patel: can you repeat the KV thing? we had notes that K-V cash was doing well but sometimes it drops.
[00:02:17] Samir (SE): sure — sorry the transcript might say K-V cash — the runtime keeps a KV cache of past attention states. dedicated pools keep that cache warm per tenant; on shared hosted it might get evicted more often under burst. so for bursty QPS and long contexts, dedicated helps.
[00:02:36] [00:02:55] Alex (AE): janelle, what timeline do you need for PO? mid-oct?
[00:03:01] Janelle Kim: mid-oct is ideal. legal needs 2 weeks review for amendments, procurement needs final numbers.
[00:03:09] Evan Torres: also need SOC2 evidence and KMS/HSM details for the pilot (we host PHI).
[00:03:16] Alex (AE): absolutely. we'll attach SOC2 report and a security addendum. Samir — can you outline KMS options?
[00:03:22] Samir (SE): yes — we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations — AWS KMS, GCP KMS, plus HSM-backed flows for Private deployments. for Hosted Dedicated we can enable encryption-at-rest with CMK and audit logs. note: for full onprem air-gapped you'll want the Private package which includes local KMS/HSM integration.
[00:03:42] [00:04:10] Dr. Mira Patel: what's the latency delta we should expect for Ireland nodes vs US-east? our tests show +30-40ms network, but overall p95 is our concern.
[00:04:22] Samir (SE): network adds ~30-40ms as you said. dedicated in-eu will give you better p95 because of consistent scheduling and local KV caching; we can target 200ms p50 and 400ms p95 for your profile assuming similar batching. we'll need to run a short perf test to validate.
[00:04:41] Alex (AE): ok so pilot plan: spin up small dedicated pool in eu-west (ireland), run bench for 48 hours with your QPS profile, then review metrics. timeline target week of oct 11?
[00:04:56] Evan Torres: that works. what's the minimum commitment?
[00:05:01] Alex (AE): for Dedicated we usually do a 3-month minimum for pilot pools to cover provisioning. pricing tiers included in the spreadsheet i'll send. we can architect a ramp with staged billing so you're not fully committed upfront.
[00:05:13] [00:05:40] Janelle Kim: please put that in writing. we need an estimated monthly cost and a sample amendment language for legal.
[00:05:48] Alex (AE): will do. Samir, can you capture the perf script link in the notes?
[00:05:54] Samir (SE): yep — i'll drop a link to our benchmark repo and a sample loader CSV. also note — if you want private onprem later, there are extra steps for audit logging and cert rotations.
[00:06:10] Dr. Mira Patel: question — competitors keep pitching lower per-token cost by using heavier quantization. how do you recommend we think about quality regression risk?
[00:06:21] Samir (SE): good point. our Optimize toolkit can run quality regressions against your eval prompts. we typically recommend running a shadowed quantization pass — run a batch of responses at int8 and compare against baseline with automated metrics and human review. if the model degrades on key prompts we keep higher precision for those routes.
[00:06:40] [00:07:05] Evan Torres: we also want to ensure audit logs are tenant-separated. we had an issue with another vendor where logs were confusing because multi-tenant metadata was stripped.
[00:07:14] Samir (SE): audit logs are tenant-scoped. for Dedicated and Private we can retain full token-level logs tied to request IDs; retention period configurable. we'll include a sample retention policy in the security pack.
[00:07:30] [00:08:00] Dr. Mira Patel: about data residency — could we test a scenario where inference stays in-eu end-to-end? network and model hosting?
[00:08:09] Alex (AE): yes — the Dedicated EU pool keeps inference within the region. for Private onprem you'd be fully localized. we'll map the traffic flow in the docs.
[00:08:18] Janelle Kim: legal will want a clause about data residency and breach notification SLA — can you provide suggested language?
[00:08:25] Alex (AE): yes, standard addendum covers breach notif windows; i'll have legal draft language.
[00:08:35] [00:09:15] Evan Torres: another technical thing — can we do a canary routing where some percentage hits hosted and the rest hits dedicated? we'd like to fail back to hosted if dedicated has incidents.
[00:09:25] Samir (SE): absolutely — routing policies support percentage-based rollouts and automatic fallback to compatible model variants. we can set policies for latency or error thresholds.
[00:09:40] [00:10:00] Dr. Mira Patel: for the pilot, i want to validate output quality doesn't regress for clinical prompts. we'll give you a 200 prompt eval set. can Redwood run continuous regression alerts?
[00:10:10] Samir (SE): yes — Redwood Optimize supports eval-based regression alerts tied to prompt sets, with thresholds and samples for triage. we'll onboard the eval set and configure alerts.
[00:10:22] [00:10:55] Alex (AE): ok so to recap: 1) Alex to send pricing + amendment template; 2) Samir share benchmark script + repo; 3) Lynwood to share QPS profile and eval prompts; 4) schedule kickoff week of Oct 11. anything missing?
[00:11:08] Janelle Kim: please add expected provisioning lead time for the EU dedicated nodes. procurement needs that for planning.
[00:11:15] Samir (SE): provisioning time around 7-10 business days once commit is signed for EU dedicated nodes; if we do a Private onprem pilot that's separate timeline.
[00:11:27] [00:11:50] Evan Torres: one more — encryption at transit and rest — confirm TLS and CMK?
[00:11:56] Samir (SE): yes TLS in transit; CMK for at rest; HSM available for Private. we'll include key rotation cadence in the security doc.
[00:12:10] [00:12:40] Dr. Mira Patel: any gotchas on model pinning and rollouts? we've had regressions when vendor rolled model behind an alias.
[00:12:48] Samir (SE): you can pin versions per route and Redwood supports canary and A/B rollouts. also automatic fallback to previous known-good variant is possible if regression triggers. we'll show example config.
[00:13:05] [00:13:40] Janelle Kim: timeline check — if we sign amendment by Oct 15, provision start is Oct 26? that's fine.
[00:13:47] Alex (AE): yes that aligns; i will plan for provisioning around oct 26.
[00:13:55] [00:14:20] Evan Torres: budget — can you provide amortized cost per 1M tokens for dedicated eu and hosted eu with VPC? we need line items for compute, storage, and premium ops.
[00:14:30] Alex (AE): yes, i'll include amortized numbers in the spreadsheet and highlight per-token delta and fixed monthly overhead.
[00:14:45] [00:15:15] Samir (SE): note: caching effectiveness can change per workload; if you have a high prefix reuse you'll see lower per-token costs on dedicated thanks to KV hits. we'll quantify that in the perf run.
[00:15:30] Dr. Mira Patel: good. question about auditability: can we get token-level tracing attached to our request IDs for a 90-day retention?
[00:15:39] Samir (SE): yes for Dedicated and Private we can do token-level tracing with configurable retention; hosted plans can also get token-level logs via add-on. we will indicate storage implications.
[00:15:52] [00:16:20] Alex (AE): ok finalizing next steps — i'll send pricing + amendment draft by monday (Oct 5), samir will share perf tools by thursday (Oct 1), and you (Lynwood) will share QPS + evals by Oct 4. pilot kickoff week of Oct 11.
[00:16:35] Janelle Kim: legal will still need sample SOW language.
[00:16:42] Alex (AE): yep we'll include sample SOW + provisioning lead times.
[00:16:48] [00:17:10] Dr. Mira Patel: one last minor thing: competitor Nimbus supposedly offers 99.9% uptime at lower cost but had opaque routing. any SLA differences to highlight?
[00:17:21] Samir (SE): Redwood SLAs vary by product — Hosted has uptime SLA, Dedicated has stronger latency and availability commitments and a premium SLA with credits. i can pull the SLA table into the pack.
[00:17:35] [00:18:00] Evan Torres: ok thanks team. we'll review the materials and circle back with PO timeline.
[00:18:07] Alex (AE): thanks everyone. i'll follow up in email with the attachments.
[00:18:12] [End of recorded transcript — remainder is Q&A offline]

Notes: occasional transcription errors present; proper nouns may be slightly off. Links shared during call: pricing-spreadsheet.xlsx (to be sent), perf-benchmarks repo link (to be shared by Samir).
